body: The contextual attributes (endpoint, pluginId, dsName, dsUID, uname) used to be set in the first middleware that runs after tracing. Now they're only added below the metrics middleware, so anything the tracing or metrics middleware logs (or passes on through ctx) no longer carries them. The LoggerMiddleware now relies on the `"Plugin Request Completed"` line getting pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsUID only from ctx. That makes the log line depend on middleware order: if someone reorders the list or builds a chain without NewContextualLoggerMiddleware (e.g. in tests or another decorator), those fields silently disappear from the grafana-data-egress log. Consider putting the contextual logger middleware right after tracing, as it was before, and noting the ordering requirement in a comment.

This removes the explicit `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `traceID` params and relies on `FromContext` to add them. `traceID` now only shows up if `tracing.ProvideService` has registered its contextual log provider, and the other fields only show up if ContextualLoggerMiddleware ran earlier in the chain. `grafana-data-egress` is an audit-style event that downstream tooling may parse, so a silent drop is a behaviour regression. Also, nothing covers this: there's no test for LoggerMiddleware or ContextualLoggerMiddleware asserting the fields are still logged.

`FromContext` returns a brand-new TestLogger instead of `f` (or something that records into `f`). Anything that now logs through `logger.FromContext(ctx)`, like LoggerMiddleware, writes to a throwaway logger, so tests that inject a TestLogger and assert on `InfoLogs.Calls` / `Message` will never see those calls. It should return `f` so calls stay observable.

`ConcreteLogger.FromContext` always returns either `cl` or `cl.New(...)`, both `*ConcreteLogger`, so this fallback is dead code today. If it ever runs, `d.New()` silently drops all the context attributes instead of failing loudly. Either keep the type as the `log.Logger` interface in the wrapper, or at least fall back to `d` rather than creating a new logger with no context.

The doc comment is copy-pasted from `New`. It should say this returns a logger enriched with the contextual attributes and trace ID from the provided `context.Context`. Also, adding a method to the exported `Logger` interface breaks every external implementation of `plog.Logger`. That's fine if it's intentional, but worth calling out.

The file and helper were renamed, but the test function is still `TestInstrumentationMiddleware`. Rename it to `TestMetricsMiddleware` for consistency. The contextual-logger behaviour that used to live in this middleware now has no tests at all.
